root_cause.text: The drm/xe exec queue initialization error path in `__xe_exec_queue_init()` failed to call `q->ops->fini()` after queue init had already registered the queue/GUC ID, leaving a partially initialized `xe_exec_queue` in GuC `exec_queue_lookup` and causing stale references.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states that “Every call to queue init should have a corresponding fini call,” that skipping it “mean[s] skipping removal of the queue from GuC list (which is part of guc_id allocation),” and the patch changes the `err_lrc` path from only releasing LRCs to calling `__xe_exec_queue_fini(q)`, which invokes `q->ops->fini(q)` before `xe_lrc_put()`; it also makes `xe_lrc_put()` NULL-safe to support cleanup of partially initialized queues.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add execution-queue finalization logic that invokes backend cleanup and releases all LRC references to prevent resource leaks.
intent_record.what: A new static helper function named __xe_exec_queue_fini was added. It takes a struct xe_exec_queue pointer, calls q->ops->fini(q), then iterates from 0 to q->width - 1 and calls xe_lrc_put(q->lrc[i]) for each entry.
intent_record.how: This adds an explicit teardown path for execution queues that runs queue-specific finalization logic and releases all LRC references associated with the queue, enabling proper cleanup of allocated resources during shutdown or error handling and preventing leaked references.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the common exec queue finalization path on init failure so partially initialized queues are fully cleaned up instead of only releasing LRCs.
intent_record.what: In the error path of __xe_exec_queue_init(), the manual loop that decremented i and called xe_lrc_put(q->lrc[i]) for previously initialized LRCs was replaced with a call to __xe_exec_queue_fini(q), and the local static definition of __xe_exec_queue_fini() was removed from its previous location in the file.
intent_record.how: On initialization failure after some resources have been set up, cleanup now goes through the shared finalization helper instead of only releasing the partially created LRC entries. This makes the error path perform the full queue teardown logic, including q->ops->fini(q), preventing incomplete cleanup and keeping failure handling consistent with normal finalization.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a NULL check in xe_lrc_put() to avoid dereferencing a NULL lrc pointer when releasing a reference.
intent_record.what: The function xe_lrc_put() was modified to wrap the existing kref_put(&lrc->refcount, xe_lrc_destroy) call in an if (lrc) conditional, so the reference count decrement and destroy callback are only invoked when the lrc pointer is non-NULL.
intent_record.how: At runtime, xe_lrc_put() now safely accepts a NULL lrc argument and does nothing instead of dereferencing lrc and crashing. This prevents NULL pointer dereference faults when callers pass a NULL pointer.

consistency_review.core_intent: Ensure partially initialized execution queues are fully cleaned up on initialization failure by routing teardown through the common finalization path and releasing all associated resources.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly address the init-error cleanup bug: they ensure failed exec queue initialization goes through the full finalization path, including backend q->ops->fini()-style cleanup and releasing LRC/resources, which matches the root cause of leaving a partially initialized queue registered in GuC state.

The change only adds a NULL check in xe_lrc_put() for safe pointer dereference during release. It does not address the exec queue initialization error path, missing q->ops->fini() call, or stale GuC exec_queue_lookup registration/root cause.

candidates.rationale: This error-path loop only released LRC references and did not invoke the queue backend finalization, so any queue/GUC ID registration performed earlier remained intact, leaving stale entries in exec_queue_lookup.

The init failure cleanup was limited to dropping LRC references. By cleaning up only LRCs and omitting q->ops->fini(), the code failed to unregister or undo backend state for a partially initialized exec queue.
Returning directly from the err_lrc path after only partial cleanup allowed initialization to fail without running the common exec queue finalization path, preserving stale backend registration.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement is the core of the flawed init failure cleanup: it only drops LRC references, but does not invoke the queue backend finalization that would unregister any queue/GUC ID state already established during initialization. As a result, partially initialized exec queues could remain referenced in GuC exec_queue_lookup.

This direct return exits the error path immediately after partial cleanup, preventing the common exec queue finalization path from running. That omission leaves backend registration intact for a queue whose initialization failed, causing stale references.

This loop structure embodies the incomplete error handling path that iterates only to release LRCs rather than funneling cleanup through the full exec queue finalization logic. It is part of the vulnerable sequence that leaves backend queue/GUC registration uncleared.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it includes the full body of the newly introduced `__xe_exec_queue_init(struct xe_exec_queue *q)` and the surrounding create/free paths. The root cause is an init error path that must call `q->ops->fini()` if queue init had already registered queue/GUC state. In this commit, `__xe_exec_queue_init()` performs initialization via `q->ops->init(q)` after LRC setup, but its only error cleanup path is `err_lrc`, which only runs `xe_lrc_finish()` in a loop and then `return err;`. There is no call to `q->ops->fini(q)` anywhere in `__xe_exec_queue_init()`'s failure handling. Specifically, after `err = q->ops->init(q); if (err) goto err_lrc;`, the `err_lrc:` label does only `for (i = i - 1; i >= 0; --i) xe_lrc_finish(q->lrc + i); return err;`. The outer caller `xe_exec_queue_create()` then handles failure with `err_post_alloc:` and calls only `__xe_exec_queue_free(q);`, which merely does `if (q->vm) xe_vm_put(q->vm); kfree(q);`. Since neither the init error path nor the post-alloc free path invokes `q->ops->fini()`, a partial `q->ops->init()` that registered the queue/GUC ID would not be undone. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix is not yet included.
